messages:
elaine: Heads-up — proposal to introduce a TF modules lockfile (modules.lock.hcl-style) + per-environment lock overrides to prevent cross-env drift for gpupool/vpc/iam/kms. Short explainer below.

rohan: +1 on having a reproducible module set. Curious how you see per-env overrides working — separate lockfile per env in repo? :eyes: 

elaine: yep, single canonical modules.lock at root, and a small optional modules.lock.<env> (e.g., modules.lock.prod) that overrides versions we explicitly want pinned in prod. GitOps pipeline picks env-specific lock during apply.

mike: question: how do we handle breaking module bumps that change resource shapes (eg. gpupool -> new subresource causes replace)? We can't force-recreate GPU pools during business hours.

elaine: plan: require a migration tag on module bump PRs. If a bump implies deletes/replaces, QE + SRE run a staged migration in staging, then do a controlled canary in us-west1 with auto-rollback. Add `apply_safe` step that checks `terraform plan` output for `-/+` or `-/` and blocks unless manual approval.

tim: CI suggestion: add `tf-drift-check` job that compares live state with plan and fails on unknown drift of critical resources (gpupool, kms_key). We can use `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` and parse.

rohan: also need provider version pinning (gcp/aws) and provider aliasing for regional work. I've seen provider upgrades silently change default networking behaviour.

ci-bot: ACTION: added pipeline job template `tf-module-lock-apply` to infra-pipeline repo — requires `manual` for any plan that touches `google_compute_instance_group_manager` or `redwood_gpupool`.

sre-oncall: reminder: draining / scaling GPU nodegroups must use our node-drain hook; ensure module exposes `pre_destroy_hook` so GitOps can trigger a safe drain before delete. Otherwise users will lose inference capacity.

mike: cost note: if we pin to older, non-quantized AMIs for gpupool we may pay ~15% more. Ops should add a cost test in CI that flags >10% unit-cost variance after bump.

elaine: agreed. next steps: I'll open a PR with RFC + example modules.lock, pipeline changes, and a short migration playbook. Targeting rollforward window next Tue 10:00 PT. @rohan @mike please review.

rohan: will review. if we can automate the per-env lock selection in Flux kustomize overlays that'd be ideal.

tim: fyi add policy checks to block KMS key reassignments without a security approval (policy sig).

mike: :thumbsup: thanks. If we need a quick hack, we can add a pre-apply job to check `count` diffs for `gpupool` and abort if >0.

elaine: thanks all — will drop link to PR here when ready. :shipit:

---

elaine: example module snippet I'll include in the RFC:

```hcl
module "gpupool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.internal/redwood/modules.git//gpupool?ref=v1.4.0"
  # versions recorded in modules.lock.*
  region = var.region
  pre_destroy_hook = local.node_drain_hook
}
```

rohan: this looks good. one more ask: include a short rollback playbook for cases where plan indicates replace of a kube nodepool resource — we should be able to abort and revert to previous module ref from the lockfile.

elaine: will add rollback steps + CLI commands to revert the modules.lock file and trigger a redeploy from the last good tag. Also adding a note about state import: if a migration requires resource import, we'll include `tf state mv`/`import` snippets.

sre-oncall: we should also add an alert to PagerDuty when a module bump PR touches >2 regions or makes >1 gpupool change. automated triage will help reduce oncall surprises.

mike: ACK. I'll add a small cost/regression check script in the infra repo to run after apply in staging.

elaine: PR target created: infra/rfcs#314 (will link once opened).
